question.text:
CONSIDER THE ENTRIES SHOWN BELOW IN THE FORWARDING TABLE OF AN IP ROUTER. EACH ENTRY CONSISTS OF AN IP PREFIX AND THE CORRESPONDING NEXT HOP ROUTER. THE NOTATION '/N' IN A PREFIX INDICATES A SUBNET MASK WITH THE MOST SIGNIFICANT $N$ BITS SET TO $1.$

\begin{array}{ll}
\text { Prefix } & \text { Next hop router } \\
172.20 .128 .0 / 19 & \text { R1 } \\
172.20 .160 .0 / 20 & \text { R2 } \\
172.20 .175 .0 / 24 & \text { R3 } \\
0.0 .0 .0 / 0 & \text { R4 }
\end{array}

THIS ROUTER FORWARDS 6 PACKETS. THE DESTINATION IP ADDRESSES OF THE PACKETS ARE:

  1. $172.20 .150 .10$
     
  2. $172.20 .170 .5$
     
  3. $172,20,175,50$
     
  4. $172.20 .190 .1$
     
  5. $172.20 .160 .200$
     
  6. $192.168.1.1$

THE NUMBER OF PACKETS FORWARDED VIA THE NEXT HOP ROUTER R2 IS ________.

question.text:
FOR A HOST MACHINE THAT USES THE TOKEN BUCKET ALGORITHM, TOKENS ARRIVE AT A RATE TO SUSTAIN A DATA RATE OF $20$ MEGABYTES PER SECOND. THE MAXIMUM OUTPUT RATE OF THE HOST IS $50$ MEGABYTES PER SECOND.

THE MACHINE MUST BE ABLE TO TRANSMIT $300$ MEGABYTES OF DATA IN A TOTAL TIME OF EXACTLY $14$ SECONDS.

THE MINIMUM CAPACITY (IN MEGABYTES) OF THE TOKEN BUCKET REQUIRED TO ACHIEVE THIS IS $\_\_\_\_$ .

question.text:
CONSIDER THREE MACHINES, P, Q, AND R, WITH IP ADDRESSES $192.168.10.130$, $192.168.10.190$, AND $192.168.10.220$ RESPECTIVELY. THE SUBNET MASK IS SET TO $255.255.255.240$ FOR ALL THREE MACHINES. WHICH ONE OF THE FOLLOWING IS TRUE?

  1. P, Q, AND R ALL BELONG TO THE SAME SUBNET.
     
  2. ONLY P AND Q BELONG TO THE SAME SUBNET.
     
  3. ONLY Q AND R BELONG TO THE SAME SUBNET.
     
  4. P, Q, AND R BELONG TO THREE DIFFERENT SUBNETS.

question.text:
A SENDER USES THE STOP-AND-WAIT ARQ PROTOCOL.

  • THE SIZE OF A DATA FRAME IS $\mathbf{2000}$ BYTES.
     
  • THE SIZE OF AN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS $\mathbf{50}$ BYTES.
     
  • THE ONE-WAY PROPAGATION DELAY IS $\mathbf{1 5 0}$ MILLISECONDS.
     
  • THE RECEIVER'S TRANSMISSION RATE IS $1/10$TH OF THE SENDER'S TRANSMISSION RATE.
     
  • ASSUME NO FRAME IS LOST AND PROCESSING DELAYS ARE NEGLIGIBLE.
     

TO ACHIEVE A SENDER THROUGHPUT OF EXACTLY $5000$ BYTES/SECOND, THE SENDER'S TRANSMISSION RATE MUST BE $\_\_\_\_$ KBPS ( $1$ KBPS $=1000$ BITS/SECOND).

question.text:
Consider a network that uses Ethernet and IPv4. Assume that IPv4 headers do not use any options field.
Each Ethernet frame can carry a maximum of $1600$ bytes in its data field.
A UDP segment is transmitted, and the payload (data) in the UDP segment is $8200$ bytes.

Which ONE of the following choices gives the correct total number of fragments transmitted and the size of the last fragment (including IPv4 header)?

  1. $5$ fragments, $1400$ bytes
     
  2. $6$ fragments, $348$ bytes
     
  3. $6$ fragments, $160$ bytes
     
  4. $7$ fragments, $80$ bytes
